entries.topic: How the dead of Gaza are counted

claims.text: Spagat et al., Lancet Global Health (Feb 2026): face-to-face survey of 2,000 households by PCPSR from 30 Dec 2024; ~75,200 violent deaths in first 15 months vs ~49,000 reported; ~16,300 non-violent excess deaths; 56.2% of violent deaths women, children, elderly; 3–4% of population killed violently by 5 Jan 2025; first independent mortality survey.

Airwars matched 2,236 of 2,993 named civilians (75%) killed 7–24 Oct 2023 to the ministry's first list; found it broadly reliable for that period; later recording weakened as hospitals stopped reporting.

The ministry published names after Biden said he had 'no confidence' in the figures; health workers record deaths in facilities; ministry does not separate combatants; Spagat: ID matching weakened after 26 Oct 2023.

Jan 2026: a senior Israeli military official said the IDF believes ~70,000 were killed (ministry 71,667); ministry records include names and IDs for over 90% of bodies; IDF said before ceasefire it killed at least 22,000 combatants; earlier IDF officials cited 2–3 civilians per combatant; official rejected the ministry's malnutrition deaths; Hamas estimates ~10,000 under rubble.
IDF spokesman Nadav Shoshani said reports the army had accepted the toll 'do not reflect official data'.

Guardian/+972/Local Call (21 Aug 2025): a classified IDF database listed 8,900 Hamas and PIJ fighters as dead or probably dead by May 2025, against at least 53,000 deaths — implying ~83% civilians; IDF said the figures were 'incorrect'.

Critique (HonestReporting): the database covers only named, confirmed operatives; unidentified fighters counted as civilians; using 22,000 operatives and 62,000 deaths gives about 2 civilians per combatant.
April 2026: about 10,000 missing believed under rubble; 759 bodies recovered; heavy machinery not admitted; over 61 million tonnes of rubble (UN).
